title: Understanding the Pharmacist Salary Melbourne: Award Rates and Calculations
description: Learn about pharmacist salary Melbourne based on Fair Work award rates, including hourly rates, annual pay, casual loading, superannuation, and tax estimates for 2026-27.
salarySummary: For a Pharmacist under the Pharmacy Industry Award, the minimum hourly rate is $41.74, leading to an annual gross salary of approximately $82,500 based on a 38-hour week.

faqs.q: How does casual loading affect a pharmacist's pay in Melbourne?
faqs.a: Casual employees under the Pharmacy Industry Award receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Pharmacist, that means $52.18 per hour instead of $41.74. The casual loading is included in penalty rates for casuals but is not payable on overtime. This loading compensates for entitlements like paid leave that casuals do not receive.

faqs.q: What superannuation contributions apply to a pharmacist salary in Melbourne?
faqs.a: Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% of ordinary earnings on top of the pharmacist's salary. For a full-time Pharmacist earning the award minimum of $82,500 annually, that adds about $9,900 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from the employee's pay; it is an additional cost to the employer.

faqs.q: How is tax calculated on a pharmacist salary in Melbourne for 2026-27?
faqs.a: Using the 2026-27 resident tax rates, a Pharmacist earning $82,500 would pay no tax on the first $18,200, then 15% on the next $26,800 ($4,020), and 30% on the remaining $37,500 ($11,250), plus a 2% Medicare levy ($1,650). Total tax and Medicare would be approximately $16,920, leaving a take-home pay of about $65,580. This estimate uses the single Medicare reduction thresholds from 2025-26.

bodyMarkdown:
## Introduction

When researching a **pharmacist salary Melbourne**, it's essential to start with the minimum rates set by the Pharmacy Industry Award 2020. These rates, updated from 1 July 2026, provide a baseline for full-time, part-time, and casual pharmacists. While actual salaries may be higher depending on experience, location, and employer, the award ensures a legal minimum. This article explains how to convert those hourly rates into annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and covers casual loading, superannuation, and tax.

## Award Rates for Pharmacists in Melbourne

The Fair Work Ombudsman's Pharmacy Industry Award pay guide lists minimum rates for several pharmacist classifications. For a standard **Pharmacist**, the minimum hourly rate is $41.74, with a weekly rate of $1,586.30 for 38 ordinary hours. An **Experienced Pharmacist** earns $45.72 per hour ($1,737.40 weekly), a **Pharmacist in Charge** $46.80 per hour ($1,778.40 weekly), and a **Pharmacist Manager** $52.15 per hour ($1,981.60 weekly). These rates apply across Australia, including Melbourne, and are reviewed annually by the Fair Work Commission.

## Calculating Annual Pay from Hourly Rate

To estimate annual gross pay, use the formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. For a full-time Pharmacist working 38 hours per week: $41.74 × 38 × 52 = $82,478.24, rounded to about $82,500. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. The fortnightly pay is simply the weekly rate doubled: $1,586.30 × 2 = $3,172.60. For part-time employees, multiply the agreed weekly hours by 52. Always check your actual hours against the award's maximum of 12 hours per day and 38 per week (or 76 over two weeks).

## Casual Loading and Its Impact

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. For a Pharmacist, that means $41.74 × 1.25 = $52.18 per hour. This loading is inclusive of penalty rates for casuals (see Table 6 of the award) but is not paid on overtime. A casual Pharmacist working 38 hours per week would earn $52.18 × 38 × 52 ≈ $103,100 annually, though casual hours are often less predictable. The loading compensates for the lack of paid leave entitlements. For more on casual pay, see our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) topic.

## Superannuation and Tax Considerations

Superannuation guarantee contributions are 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top of the salary. For a Pharmacist earning $82,500, the employer adds about $9,900 in super, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Super is not deducted from your pay; it's an additional cost to the employer. For tax, the 2026-27 resident rates apply: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on the next $26,800, 30% on the next $90,000, and so on. A single Pharmacist earning $82,500 would pay approximately $16,920 in tax and Medicare levy (2%), leaving a take-home pay of about $65,580. This estimate uses the 2025-26 Medicare reduction thresholds. For a detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

## Comparing with Other Pay Measures

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $33.05 with casual loading. A Pharmacist's award rate of $41.74 is well above that. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time employees was $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to about $108,350 annually. A Pharmacist at the award minimum earns less than this average, reflecting that many pharmacists progress to higher classifications or negotiate above-award rates. For reference, our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page discusses broader earnings data.

## Conclusion

Understanding the **pharmacist salary Melbourne** starts with the award minimums, but actual pay can vary. Use the formula hourly × 38 × 52 to estimate annual gross, add super at 12%, and apply tax rates for net pay. For casual roles, remember the 25% loading. Always consult the latest [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data) from the Fair Work Ombudsman for updates. This estimate is a starting point; your actual pay may differ based on your employment agreement and circumstances.
